text:
lee: hey team, day 1 and hitting a weird one. i'm on company macbook (Ventura) with the split-tunnel WireGuard profile. i need to reach our internal artifact service at artifacts.vpce.internal (it's an AWS VPC endpoint), but `curl https://artifacts.vpce.internal` just hangs. i can ssh to bastion.redwood and curl from there succeeds. any quick ideas?

mira: welcome @lee! quick checks: what does `dig +short artifacts.vpce.internal` return on your laptop vs the bastion? also which WG profile did you import?

lee: dig on laptop returns nothing. on bastion `dig +short artifacts.vpce.internal` -> 10.20.33.10. using the standard onboarding wg profile.

dev-mentor: sounds like the split-DNS for VPC endpoints isn't in the profile. VPC endpoints use private hosted zones in Route53 and the VPN needs to push the resolver or the zone entries. short-term workaround: two options: 1) SSH local port forward to the bastion `ssh -L 8443:10.20.33.10:443 ubuntu@bastion.redwood` then point requests to https://localhost:8443 (beware TLS SAN), or 2) use a SOCKS proxy `ssh -D 1080 ubuntu@bastion.redwood` and set `ALL_PROXY=socks5h://127.0.0.1:1080` so DNS happens over the tunnel.

lee: i tried `ssh -L` and `curl -k https://localhost:8443` returns the artifact index. npm/yarn still fail because of cert hostname mismatch.

mira: hosts file won't help TLS for internal certs. for TLS you can either: a) use `ssh -L` and point client config to localhost (if the client allows overriding host) or b) temporarily install the internal CA into macOS keychain and Docker/Node cert store (ops/security may not love that).

dev-mentor: another trick: use `ssh -J ubuntu@bastion.redwood git@artifacts.vpce.internal` style ProxyJump for git/ssh protocols. For web APIs that require TLS SNI to match the original hostname, you can run a reverse proxy on the bastion (nginx) bound to localhost:someport and forward to the VPC endpoint, then `ssh -L` to that local port; the bastion's nginx can present the internal cert if available. messy but works for day-zero.

lee: is there a way to avoid manual tunnels? i don't want to babysit this every morning.

mira: netops needs to add the Route53 private zone resolver to the WireGuard profile (push the VPC resolver IP and domain search for `vpce.internal`), that's the long-term fix. i'll open a ticket. also for persistence you can use `~/.ssh/config` + `autossh` and `launchd` so the tunnel runs at login automatically.

netops-bot: creating ticket #11021: "Include Route53 private zone resolver + vpce.internal in new-hire WireGuard split-DNS" assigned to @netops. ETA 2 business days.

it-bot: created ticket #11021 and linked onboarding doc PR template.

lee: thanks. one more weirdness: when i tried to use `kubectl port-forward` from my laptop to a pod that pulls artifacts from artifacts.vpce.internal, the pod couldn't resolve the host either. is that expected?

dev-mentor: kubectl port-forward doesn't change cluster DNS; the pod's environment and the cluster's VPC must resolve the endpoint. if the pod talks to the VPC endpoint from inside the cluster, that's fine; the issue you're seeing is when you try to port-forward an app that itself does outbound lookups from your laptop context. port-forward is only a TCP tunnel to the pod, DNS resolution still happens where the process runs. when in doubt, run the command inside the pod (`kubectl exec`) to test DNS from the pod network.

mira: good call. i'll add a quick note to the onboarding VPN doc: 1) how to test resolution (`dig`) locally vs bastion, 2) ssh -L and ssh -D workarounds, 3) persistence via autossh/launchd, 4) why hosts file won't fix TLS, and 5) that kubectl port-forward doesn't magically fix cluster DNS issues.

lee: super helpful, thanks everyone 60a i'll use the tunnel for now and follow the ticket. appreciate the warm welcome!
